claims.text: The starting TiVNbTa alloy has a single-phase BCC dendritic structure.
The starting TiVNbTa alloy has a low-temperature yield strength of approximately 800 MPa.
At 1273 K, the TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa.
At 1273 K and 30% strain, the TiVNbTa alloy has a compressive strength of approximately 423 MPa.
Adding a small, controlled amount of Y2O3 during processing will mitigate the high-temperature strength loss of TiVNbTa.
Mechanical alloying or an equivalent dispersion technique can produce a fine, uniform dispersion of Y2O3 particles in the TiVNbTa matrix.
The intervention produces nanoscale Y2O3 particles uniformly dispersed within TiVNbTa.
Dispersed oxide particles inhibit dislocation motion at elevated temperature.
Dispersed oxide particles inhibit grain-boundary sliding at elevated temperature.
Inhibition of dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding increases high-temperature yield and compressive strength.
The ODS TiVNbTa variant is expected to have a higher yield strength than the baseline alloy at 1273 K.
The ODS TiVNbTa variant is expected to have a higher compressive strength than the baseline alloy at 1273 K.
The ODS intervention is expected to preserve the structural integrity of TiVNbTa when used as a heat-transfer layer between W and CuCrZr.
The proposed application boundary is operation near 1273 K at strains up to 30% between W and CuCrZr.
A controlled comparison of Y2O3-containing and Y2O3-free TiVNbTa specimens at 1273 K can test the hypothesis.
